clue.text: Pile of bricks left in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the word for left is placed inside the word for temporary accommodation

parts.note: a camp is a temporary place to stay

explanation.surface: A heap of bricks has been abandoned inside a makeshift encampment.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a stack of bricks piled up for firing, a builder's technical sense.

clue.text: After course of study, struggle to receive thanks —— the story of my life!

indicators.note: the second piece follows the course of study

parts.note: a curriculum is a course of study

indicators.note: the struggle word takes in the thanks word

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over their life after years of study and effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Curriculum vitae is Latin for course of life, a written account of one's career.

clue.text: Fabulous writer's uplifting main work

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the main is the open sea
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A writer's inspiring major work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means writing fables, not marvellous; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables, so a writer of fables.

clue.text: Dancing companion sometimes joining in crime

definitions.meaning: an accomplice, from the phrase used of a fellow criminal

explanation.definitionFit: A partner is the person one dances with, and an accomplice is a partner in crime.

clue.text: Animal spray, a thing racketeers hope to make fast

parts.note: spraying something is watering it

parts.words: a thing racketeers hope to make fast
parts.note: racketeers want to make a fast buck, quick dishonest money

explanation.surface: An animal is sprayed while crooks scheme to earn money quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' does not describe the making; the idiom is 'make a fast buck', and BUCK is the thing made.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterbuck is a large African antelope, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Hazard in northern river, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this signals that a word is spoken, not written

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England, through Durham

explanation.surface: A danger lurks in a river in the north, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam across a river, a hazard to boats and swimmers.

clue.text: Gigantic, like some redheads in paintings I abandoned

indicators.note: I abandoned means the letter standing for I is deserted and left out of the painterly word

parts.note: Titian painted women with auburn hair, now called Titian red

explanation.surface: Huge, like painted auburn beauties, says an artist giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanesque means like a Titan, the giants of Greek myth, so gigantic.

clue.text: Seventh heaven modified for Nanki-Poo?

definitions.meaning: in The Mikado, Nanki-Poo sings of his 'modified' delight

explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is ecstatic joy, and Nanki-Poo exclaims 'Modified rapture!' in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera The Mikado.

clue.text: Mysteriously beheaded Scottish king? Nothing unknown

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is cut off

parts.note: Duncan was the king of Scotland killed by Macbeth
nil means nothing
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A Scottish king loses his head in a strange way, leaving nothing known.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncannily means in a strange, weird way, a synonym for mysteriously.

clue.text: What a child is game to be, at a push

definitions.text: What a child is game to be, at a push

parts.words: What a child is game to be, at a push
parts.note: a playground game where a child holds a mound and pushes rivals off; 'game' means willing and 'at a push' means if necessary

explanation.definitionFit: King of the castle is a children's game in which one player is pushed off the top by the others.

clue.text: Prop accepting coach's controlling influence

indicators.note: the support word takes in the coaching word, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a rest is a prop or support
to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A support takes in a trainer's steadying hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is a check that holds something back, a synonym for a controlling influence.

clue.text: Writer's taken in about nut-tree

indicators.note: the writer has taken in the word for about, so it sits inside

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement; the 's stands for has
CA (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: An author has been fooled about a particular nut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' reads as 'writer has': the pen has taken in CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a North American hickory grown for its edible nuts, so it is a nut-tree.

clue.text: One member's demise appearing to be imminent

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP is a Member of Parliament
a demise is an end or death

explanation.surface: The death of a parliamentarian looks to be close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to hang over as about to happen, a synonym for being imminent.

clue.text: Suggestion hostelry faces ruin, admitting drug

indicators.note: the hostelry stands in front of the ruin, facing it, so comes first

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry

indicators.note: the word for ruin lets the drug in, so it goes inside

parts.note: to undo someone is to ruin them
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a pub is going bust after letting drugs in.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an oblique hint or insinuation, a kind of suggestion.

clue.text: Quarters are unable to house heavyweight soldiers

indicators.note: the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: can't means are unable
a ton is a heavy weight
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Barracks can't fit a big man among the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantonment is a military station or set of quarters for troops, especially in India.

clue.text: Road liable to be accepted as adequate

parts.note: being under something, as under threat, means being liable to it
work that passes is accepted as good enough

explanation.surface: A road might just scrape through an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: An underpass is a road or path running beneath another road or railway.

clue.text: Carry out shot cashier

explanation.definitionFit: Discharge means to fulfil a duty, the firing of a weapon, and to dismiss someone from service.

clue.text: One of two writers having material rejected

indicators.note: material thrown back is read backwards

parts.note: toile is a linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: One of a pair of authors has their manuscript turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link: the writer is the material reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot is the surname of two famous writers, George Eliot and T. S. Eliot.

clue.text: Indisposition to be overcome

explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a mild ailment, and to be upset is to be overcome with feeling.

clue.text: Male bat, wild, but apt for domestication

indicators.note: wild letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A male bat is untamed yet suitable as a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamable means able to be tamed, fit to be domesticated.

clue.text: Endlessly peevish character given work in pool?

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: touchy means easily irritated, peevish
a type is a printed character

explanation.surface: A grumpy sort is given a job at the swimming baths.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is a typing pool, an office of typists, not a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch-type is to type without looking at the keys, the work done in a typing pool.

clue.text: Dull murmurous sound with percussion accompaniment

parts.note: a hum is a low murmuring sound
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A low murmur backed by drumming.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means monotonous and lacking excitement, a synonym for dull.

clue.text: Energetic escape across English border

indicators.note: the escape word stretches across the other pieces, which go inside

parts.note: a vent is an outlet or escape
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A lively breakout over the English frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and intense, close to energetic in manner.

clue.text: In Blenheim Palace one advances by leaps and bounds

definitions.text: one advances by leaps and bounds

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone makes rapid progress inside a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace is a grand country house in Oxfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope famous for its great leaps, so it literally bounds along.

clue.text: Professional terminology no judge used for rare gas

indicators.note: without the judge, so its letter is removed

parts.note: jargon is the special vocabulary of a profession

explanation.surface: Without a judge, legal jargon is used about an inert gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is one of the noble or rare gases in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Came to pass in northern mountain

definitions.meaning: a hill or mountain in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: Fell is the past of fall, meaning happened, and a fell is a northern English upland.

clue.text: One's heart may do it because of beloved's entrance

parts.note: thro', short for through, means by reason of

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lover's heart pounds at the arrival of the beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' means way in, so the first letter of 'beloved', not the verb meaning enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart beats strongly or pulses, which is exactly what it is said to do with emotion.

clue.text: Rejected article about the old brigadier's plant

indicators.note: the reversed article goes round the other pieces
turned back, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: the is the definite article
ye is an archaic form of the
Brig is the abbreviation for brigadier

explanation.surface: An old brigadier's flower is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns THE into EHT, which goes 'about' YE and BRIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower once used to treat eye complaints, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Basic points about learner with crazy ideas

indicators.note: the two compass points go round the learner

parts.note: E and E are two compass points, east
L is the learner sign on a car
mental, informally, means crazy

explanation.surface: Key arguments revolve around a student full of mad notions.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or rudimentary, a synonym for basic.

clue.text: Eastern island's first minister's residence

indicators.note: the island's name comes first, ahead of the eastern letter

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An island in the east houses its premier's official home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First minister' looks like a title; 'first' is the order signal, and the minister is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a Presbyterian or Scottish minister.
